summary: The product changes form a coherent cross-task implementation: the PG19 query/value contract, registry and recording exclusion, version-aware TUI navigation, and replay layout boundaries agree across files, and the focused tests exercise real state and behavior. Acceptance is nevertheless blocked by a destructive fixed-name shared-fixture test and by an invalid exact freeze-qa invocation in the approved decomposition. The roadmap also retains stale pre-implementation status and rejected scope/navigation statements. No scripted feature-r1 scenario and no manual SC-5 through SC-8 result is claimed; SC-9 passed for its five designated documentation/register areas, while the stale roadmap is outside that checklist.

findings.issue: Test_StatAutovacuumScoresQuery_RoundedTieRawOrder runs in the ordinary shared PG19 fixture but starts with DROP TABLE IF EXISTS over three fixed persistent public-schema names, then recreates them and drops them again during cleanup. A pre-existing object with one of those names is deleted without an ownership check, and concurrent runs can drop or replace each other's fixtures, causing cross-run data loss and nondeterministic failures. This is the same shared-fixture hazard that Task 02's security round 1 required removing; Task 01's dedicated-cluster isolation protects only the wraparound test, not this mutating test.
findings.evidence: Source inspection at lines 187-243 shows connectAutovacuumScoresFixture selecting the ordinary PG19 endpoint whenever the dedicated marker is absent, followed by unconditional fixed-name DROP TABLE IF EXISTS at lines 201-203 and 204-207, persistent CREATE TABLE statements at lines 210-217, and cleanup DROP at lines 204-207. Unlike Test_StatAutovacuumScoresQuery_WraparoundException, this test has no dedicated marker, expected system_identifier, or external supervisor. I did not execute this destructive test. A disposable shared-fixture control with a precreated sentinel of the same name, plus two concurrent invocations, would confirm the deletion/interference dynamically; the unsafe operations themselves are directly visible in the supplied source.
findings.recommendation: Remove all anticipatory and fixed-name persistent DROP statements from the shared-fixture path. Use per-session temporary relations if the autovacuum catalog supports the required fixture, or a uniquely generated per-run schema whose identifier is safely quoted and whose cleanup drops only objects owned by that run; alternatively move this mutating fixture under the same fail-closed disposable-cluster supervisor. Register cleanup immediately after successful connection and add a concurrency/ownership control. Re-run the named rounded-order test and the ORDER BY alias mutation after the fixture change.
